children: , the AI-cybersecurity platform company, entered the S&P 100 before Monday's opening bell, putting the stock directly in front of another wave of benchmark-driven capital. Shares climbed approximately 2.4% to $372.37, extending the market's willingness to pay up for large-scale cybersecurity exposure.

The bigger story remains the operating engine behind the index promotion. Palo Alto's latest quarter delivered nearly $1 billion of net new next-generation-security annual recurring revenue, pushing NGS ARR to $9.1 billion, up 63%. Remaining performance obligations reached $21.2 billion, rising 34%, giving investors another signal that demand for the company's broader security platform is still expanding at scale.

The valuation picture is much harder to ignore. At $372.37, Palo Alto trades 59.82% above its $232.99 GF Value estimate, showing how aggressively investors are already pricing in future growth. The index upgrade can boost passive ownership and liquidity, but it cannot manufacture earnings power. From here, the stock needs AI-driven security demand, stronger recurring revenue and sustained execution to keep supporting a valuation this far above its GuruFocus benchmark.

title: Palo Alto Jumps 2.4% as S&P 100 Meets AI Security Growth
